simple.meaning: אִי (ʼîy) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a howler (used only in the plural), i.e. any solitary wild creature.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.

simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.short: a howler (used only in the plural), i.e. any solitary wild creature
definitions.full: H338. i II. [ אִי ] noun masculine jackal ( howler , for * אָוִי see Ba NB 188 , compare Arabic , whence ) — plural אִיִּים , Isa 13:22 ; 34:14 ; Jer 50:39 (inhabitant of desert, ruin).
definitions.rootNote: probably identical with 337 (through the idea of a doleful sound);
